title: Ezekiel Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 5.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Take a sharp knife and a barber's razor
Bind a few hairs in thy skirts
Burn a third part with fire
Scatter a third part in the wind
questions.correctAnswer: Take a sharp knife and a barber's razor
questions.explanation: This is the first command given to Ezekiel in the chapter, as stated in Ezekiel 5:1.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel use to divide the hair?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is instructed to take balances to weigh and divide the hair in Ezekiel 5:1.

questions.question: What shall be done to a third part of the hair according to Ezekiel 5?
options: It shall be burned with fire
It shall be scattered in the wind
It shall be bound in skirts
It shall be smitten with a knife
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be burned with fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is commanded to burn a third part with fire as stated in Ezekiel 5:2.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel do with the hair that is bound in his skirts?
options: He scatters it in the wind
He burns it in the fire
He smites it with a knife
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is instructed to bind a few in his skirts as stated in Ezekiel 5:3.

questions.question: What will come forth into all the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is told that a fire shall come forth into all the house of Israel in Ezekiel 5:4.

questions.question: What city is referred to in Ezekiel 5?
questions.explanation: The Lord God refers to Jerusalem in Ezekiel 5:5.

questions.question: What has Jerusalem changed according to Ezekiel 5?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem has changed God's judgments into wickedness as stated in Ezekiel 5:6.

questions.question: What has Jerusalem refused according to Ezekiel 5?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem has refused God's judgments as stated in Ezekiel 5:6.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 5, what shall happen after the days of the siege are fulfilled?
options: A third part shall be burned
A third part shall be scattered
questions.explanation: All these actions are commanded to be done after the days of the siege are fulfilled in Ezekiel 5:2.

questions.question: The hair taken from Ezekiel's head is to be divided into how many parts?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is commanded to divide the hair into three parts as mentioned in Ezekiel 5:2.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 5, who is referred to as 'son of man'?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is addressed as 'son of man' in Ezekiel 5:1.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 5, has Jerusalem walked in God's statutes?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem has not walked in God's statutes as mentioned in Ezekiel 5:6.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 5, Jerusalem is set in the midst of the nations.
questions.explanation: The Lord God states that Jerusalem is set in the midst of the nations in Ezekiel 5:5.

questions.question: Ezekiel is instructed to take a sword to divide the hair.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is instructed to take balances to weigh and divide the hair, not a sword, as stated in Ezekiel 5:1.

questions.question: A flood will come forth into all the house of Israel according to Ezekiel 5.
questions.explanation: A fire will come forth into all the house of Israel, not a flood, as stated in Ezekiel 5:4.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen because Israel has multiplied more than the nations around her?
options: The Lord will bless her abundantly
questions.explanation: This is correct because Ezekiel 5:8 states, 'Behold, I, even I, am against thee, and will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 5:7 promise will happen if someone does not walk in God's statutes?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Ezekiel 5:7 emphasizes the consequences of not following God's statutes, leading to judgments.

questions.question: What will be the fate of a third part of the people according to Ezekiel 5:12?
options: They shall return to their land
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 5:12 clearly states that 'A third part of thee shall die with the pestilence.'

questions.question: What will happen to those who have defiled God's sanctuary according to Ezekiel 5:11?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Ezekiel 5:11 states, 'therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 5:10, what will fathers and sons do in the midst of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 5:10 states, 'the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers.'

questions.question: What is the significance of the sharp knife and barber's razor in Ezekiel 5:1?
questions.explanation: This is correct as the use of these items in Ezekiel 5:1 symbolizes the severe judgment that is to come upon Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 5:6 indicate about Israel's actions compared to the nations around her?
options: She has changed God's judgments into wickedness
questions.correctAnswer: She has changed God's judgments into wickedness
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 5:6 states that Israel has changed God's judgments into wickedness more than the nations around her.

questions.question: What will God do to the remnant of Israel according to Ezekiel 5:10?
options: He will scatter them into all the winds
questions.correctAnswer: He will scatter them into all the winds
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 5:10 mentions, 'the whole remnant of thee will I scatter into all the winds.'

questions.question: Ezekiel 5:9 mentions that God will do something He has not done before. What is it?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 5:9 states, 'I will do in thee that which I have not done.'

questions.question: What is the consequence of defiling God's sanctuary as mentioned in Ezekiel 5:11?
questions.explanation: This is correct due to the clear statement in Ezekiel 5:11, where God declares that He will diminish those who have defiled His sanctuary.

questions.question: The actions of Israel led to what specific consequence according to Ezekiel 5:12?
options: They will be protected from pestilence
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 5:12 states that 'with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of thee.'

questions.question: The statement 'I am against thee' signifies what according to Ezekiel 5:8?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Ezekiel 5:8 expresses that God is against Jerusalem to execute judgments.

questions.question: True or False: Those who refuse God's judgments will face consequences according to Ezekiel 5.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as the entire chapter emphasizes the consequences faced by those who refuse to follow God's judgments.

questions.question: True or False: God promises total protection for Israel despite their actions according to Ezekiel 5.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as the chapter outlines severe judgments and consequences due to Israel's actions.

questions.question: True or False: The judgments described in Ezekiel 5 are meant to show God's indifference to Israel's sins.
questions.explanation: This statement is false because the judgments demonstrate God's active response to Israel's sins, showing His concern for justice.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 5.

questions.question: What will the nations know when God's anger is accomplished according to Ezekiel 5:13?
options: That the LORD has spoken it in His zeal
That the nations are more powerful
That the temple will be restored
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD has spoken it in His zeal
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in Ezekiel 5:13, which states that the people shall know that the LORD has spoken it in His zeal when His fury is accomplished.

questions.question: What will God make Jerusalem according to Ezekiel 5:14?
options: A land of milk and honey
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:14 indicates that God will make Jerusalem waste and a reproach among the nations surrounding it.

questions.question: What types of judgments will God execute on Jerusalem according to Ezekiel 5:15?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:15 describes the judgments that will be executed in anger and fury as a result of Jerusalem's actions.

questions.question: What will God increase upon Jerusalem according to Ezekiel 5:16?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:16 states that God will send upon them famine and will increase it for their destruction.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 5:17, what additional calamities will God bring upon Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:17 mentions that God will send famine and evil beasts to bereave the people, along with pestilence and blood.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'zeal' in Ezekiel 5:13 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word translated as 'zeal' conveys the meaning of jealousy, indicating God's passionate commitment to His covenant.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ezekiel 5:15 with the phrase 'reproach and a taunt'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'reproach and a taunt' in Ezekiel 5:15 demonstrates parallelism, a common literary device in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment in Ezekiel 5:8?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 25:31 also speaks of God's judgment against nations, echoing the theme present in Ezekiel 5:8.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the prophecy of famine as mentioned in Ezekiel 5:16?
questions.explanation: Lamentations 4:9 speaks of the consequences of famine, fulfilling the prophecy of Ezekiel 5:16.

questions.question: What comes before God's declaration of anger in Ezekiel 5:13?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:12 discusses the abominations of the people, leading to God's declaration of anger in verse 13.

questions.question: What precedes God's statement about breaking the staff of bread in Ezekiel 5:16?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 5:17, God states that He will send famine and evil beasts, which precedes the breaking of the staff of bread in verse 16.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 5, God's judgments are a demonstration of His:
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:15 explicitly states that the judgments executed will be in anger and fury, reflecting God's righteous indignation.

questions.question: The phrase 'I the LORD have spoken it' emphasizes God's:
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase 'I the LORD have spoken it' in Ezekiel 5 underscores God's authority and sovereignty in executing His judgments.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 5 depicts God's desire for His people to return to Him.
questions.explanation: While God desires repentance, Ezekiel 5 emphasizes His impending judgment rather than an invitation to return at this moment.

questions.question: True or False: The judgments in Ezekiel 5 are meant to instruct the surrounding nations.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:15 indicates that the judgments will serve as an instruction and astonishment to the nations around Israel.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 5:6 teach about human sin?
options: Human sin involves rejecting God's judgments and statutes in favor of wickedness
Human sin is primarily about ignorance of God's law
Human sin is excusable when compared to other nations
Human sin is only about external actions, not internal attitudes
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin involves rejecting God's judgments and statutes in favor of wickedness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:6 states that Jerusalem changed God’s judgments into wickedness and refused His statutes, showing the doctrine that sin is a willful rejection and perversion of God's revealed law.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Ezekiel 5:12?
options: Divine judgment is comprehensive, affecting pestilence, famine, sword, and scattering
Divine judgment is limited to spiritual consequences only
Divine judgment is arbitrary and without pattern
Divine judgment is only temporary and superficial
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment is comprehensive, affecting pestilence, famine, sword, and scattering
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:12 outlines a multifaceted judgment involving pestilence, famine, sword, and exile, teaching that God's judgment is thorough and all-encompassing.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's holiness and justice is taught in Ezekiel 5:11?
options: God’s holiness demands that He not spare or have pity on defilement of His sanctuary
God’s holiness allows for compromise when people repent
God’s justice is flexible and changes with human will
God’s holiness is only symbolic, not active in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands that He not spare or have pity on defilement of His sanctuary
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:11 emphasizes that because Jerusalem defiled God's sanctuary, He will diminish them without sparing or pitying, showing the doctrine that God's holiness requires just judgment against sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 5:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:8 demonstrates God's sovereignty as He declares He is against Jerusalem and will execute judgments in the midst of her in full view of the nations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 5:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:13 states that God will be comforted when His fury is accomplished, showing His zeal in executing righteous judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 5:5 connect to the broader biblical theme of Jerusalem’s role among the nations?
options: It portrays Jerusalem as a divinely appointed center meant to be a light and example to surrounding nations
It shows Jerusalem as isolated and irrelevant to other nations
It emphasizes Jerusalem’s political alliances rather than spiritual significance
It denies any special role for Jerusalem among nations
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays Jerusalem as a divinely appointed center meant to be a light and example to surrounding nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:5 states that Jerusalem is set in the midst of nations, reflecting the biblical theme of Jerusalem’s central role as a spiritual and political hub.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 5:10 have with Old Testament covenant curses?
options: It echoes the covenant curses where judgment involves internal strife and exile as consequences of covenant unfaithfulness
It introduces a new kind of judgment unknown in earlier covenants
It contradicts the covenant curses by showing mercy instead of punishment
It ignores covenantal context and focuses only on political defeat
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the covenant curses where judgment involves internal strife and exile as consequences of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:10’s imagery of fathers eating sons reflects covenant curses in Deuteronomy where disobedience brings internal violence and scattering, emphasizing covenantal judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ezekiel 5:2 and Ezekiel 5:12 teach about the nature of divine judgment?
options: Divine judgment is both partial and comprehensive, involving destruction, wounding, and exile
Divine judgment is limited to physical punishment only
Divine judgment excludes exile as a penalty
Divine judgment is symbolic, with no real-world consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment is both partial and comprehensive, involving destruction, wounding, and exile
questions.explanation: Both Ezekiel 5:2 and 5:12 describe dividing the people into thirds for burning, sword, and scattering, showing that judgment is multifaceted and affects the nation in multiple ways.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 5:9 and Ezekiel 5:11 teach about the uniqueness of God’s judgment?
options: God’s judgment in this instance is unprecedented and inescapable due to abominations committed
God’s judgment is repetitive and predictable with room for leniency
God’s judgment is negotiable if the people repent quickly
God’s judgment is arbitrary and inconsistent
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment in this instance is unprecedented and inescapable due to abominations committed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:9 states God will do what He has not done before due to abominations; 5:11 emphasizes no pity will be given, highlighting the unique severity of judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 5:14 and Ezekiel 5:15 teach about the purpose of divine judgment among the nations?
options: Judgment serves as a reproach and a warning to surrounding nations, instructing them about God’s holiness
Judgment is a secret event with no public witness
Judgment is only for Israel and irrelevant to other nations
Judgment is primarily restorative and privately administered
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment serves as a reproach and a warning to surrounding nations, instructing them about God’s holiness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:14-15 describe Jerusalem becoming a taunt and instruction to nations, showing judgment’s didactic and revelatory purpose to all peoples.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Ezekiel 5:16-17 teaches God is cruel and unjust because He sends famine, beasts, pestilence, and sword indiscriminately. What does Ezekiel 5:16-17 actually teach?
options: God’s judgments are just responses to covenant unfaithfulness and serve to bring about repentance and correction
God arbitrarily punishes without cause or warning
God’s punishments are purely punitive with no redemptive purpose
God’s actions are random natural disasters with no moral significance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgments are just responses to covenant unfaithfulness and serve to bring about repentance and correction
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:16-17 shows these judgments are sent because of Israel’s sins, emphasizing divine justice and the corrective purpose of judgment in covenant context.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 5:1 teach about prophetic symbolism in divine revelation?
options: Prophetic acts serve as tangible, symbolic representations of divine judgment
Prophetic symbolism is purely decorative with no theological meaning
Prophetic acts are optional and have no bearing on the message
Prophetic symbolism is only for the prophet’s private reflection
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic acts serve as tangible, symbolic representations of divine judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:1 shows the prophet performing a symbolic act of cutting hair, representing judgment, demonstrating the use of prophetic symbolism to communicate God’s message.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 5:7 specifically highlight in relation to Israel’s sinfulness?
options: God’s justice in holding Israel accountable despite their population growth
God’s mercy in overlooking population increase
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in holding Israel accountable despite their population growth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:7 points out that Israel multiplied more than nations yet did not keep statutes, so God’s justice demands judgment regardless of numbers.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is shown in Ezekiel 5:4 with respect to the concept of purification through fire?
options: The use of fire as a purifying judgment prefigures later New Testament themes of sanctification
Fire here symbolizes only destruction with no purification
Fire is unrelated to covenant theology and is merely natural disaster
Fire is a metaphor for political upheaval only
questions.correctAnswer: The use of fire as a purifying judgment prefigures later New Testament themes of sanctification
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:4 speaks of fire coming forth into Israel’s house, linking to biblical themes where fire purifies and refines, anticipating sanctification doctrines.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 5:3 and Ezekiel 5:4 teach about the nature and extent of divine judgment?
options: Judgment includes both preservation of a remnant and destruction by fire
Judgment is exclusively total annihilation with no survivors
Judgment spares all those bound and preserves them without testing
Judgment is random and unstructured with no purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment includes both preservation of a remnant and destruction by fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:3 mentions binding a few in skirts, while 5:4 describes burning some in fire, illustrating God’s judgment balancing destruction and preservation.
